To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Carnian and Plosbachian siliciclasic deposits of the Villány Mountains are sourced from inside the South Western Tisza Mega Unit, the Upper Triassic clastics of the Mecsek are sourced from the local basement and from the Bohemian Massifs, and the 200 Ma ages are tentatively explained by synsedimentary volcanic rocks in the Central Atlantic.

the Carnian and Ppliensbachian siliciclasic deposits in the Southwestern part of the Tisaa Megaunit derive from the basement of the Slavonian Mountains, whereas the Upper Triassic deposits in the Mecsek Mountains derive from the Variscan feldspar granites or from the Bohemian Massifs.

the Upper Triassic clastics of the Mecsek and Villány Hills were derived from different sources, and the provenance of the Villány clastic deposits is more complex than the provenance of that of the Mecsek.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the paleogeographic position and evolution of the Southwestern Tisa Megaunit during the Early Mesozoicum.
the paleogeographic relation of the Southwestern Tisa Megaunit to adjacent terranes, and with the provenance of the Upper Carnian to Plienbachian clastic deposits of its western margin.
the paleogeographic evolution of the Tiszas Megaunit in the Early Mesozic era and its paleo-position in the Pannonian Basin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Tisza Megauunit formed a distinct tectonic block during the Early Mesozoics, which was separated by deep-sea from the Bohemian Massifs and the Dinarids, and from which the Southern Carpathians and the Transylvanian Basin were separated by shallow marine areas.
the Upper Triassic clastics of the Villány and Mecsek areas are not derived from the same source area.
the Tisza Megablock formed part of the European Plate during the Early Mesozoica and was located in the southernmost margin of it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Upper Triassic clastics of the Southwestern Tisa Megaunit were deposited in a foreland basin, which developed on the southern margin of Europe.
the Upper Triassic clastics of the Mecsek Mts. and Villány Hills represent a mixture of local and distal sources.
the Upper Triassic deposits of the Mecseki and Villányi Basins were sourced from the basement of the Tiszaság Unit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Southwestern Tisa Megaunit is not a fragment of the Variscan basement, as previously thought, but rather an independent tectonic block with its own basement and history.
the Tisza and Dinarid Megaunits were already connected in the Carnian.
the Tisza Megauit was not a passive margin in the Early Meszoic era, but was a part of a large-scale orogen, which was formed during the collision of the Laurasia–Gondwana supercontinent.
